query: Most of my money is in cash right now. Is that okay or should I shift it into investments?

recommendations.title: Maintain High Cash Reserves to Complete Emergency Fund
recommendations.summary: Keep 60% cash allocation until you reach your $22,000 emergency fund target, then gradually shift excess into investments.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With $15,000 in cash against a $22,000 emergency fund goal, you're 68% complete. Given your conservative risk tolerance (loss comfort 3/10), moderate debt ($38,000), and lack of a complete emergency fund, maintaining high cash reserves is appropriate. Your current cash position provides essential financial security. Once you reach $22,000 in emergency savings, you can redirect monthly surplus ($3,800 expenses vs ~$6,000 gross monthly income) into investment accounts. This strategy aligns with conservative investing principles: secure your foundation before taking market risk.
recommendations.suggested_action: Continue building cash reserves to $22,000, then begin dollar-cost averaging surplus income into VTTSX

recommendations.title: Optimize Investment Allocation After Emergency Fund Completion
recommendations.summary: Once emergency fund is established, shift to a 40% cash / 50% stocks / 10% bonds allocation to balance growth with your conservative profile.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your current 30% equity / 10% bond allocation in investments is overly conservative for a 28-year-old with stable income and a 5-7 year house down payment goal. After securing your emergency fund, a target allocation of 40% cash (emergency reserves), 50% diversified equity (VTTSX), and 10% bonds (BND) better balances safety with the growth needed for your $60,000 house goal. This allocation respects your conservative tolerance while providing reasonable growth potential (estimated 4-6% annually). The VTTSX target-date fund automatically rebalances and reduces risk over time, appropriate for your beginner experience level.
recommendations.suggested_action: After emergency fund completion, redirect monthly savings into VTTSX until reaching 50% total portfolio allocation

recommendations.title: Address Moderate Debt Before Accelerating Investments
recommendations.summary: Prioritize paying down high-interest debt alongside emergency fund building to improve net worth and reduce financial risk.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your negative net worth (-$13,000) and moderate debt load ($38,000) represent significant financial risk that should be addressed before aggressively investing. If any debt carries interest above 6-7%, paying it down provides a guaranteed 'return' that exceeds most conservative investments while reducing financial vulnerability. With $2,200 monthly surplus ($6,000 income minus $3,800 expenses), consider allocating: $1,500 to emergency fund completion, $500 to high-interest debt acceleration, and $200 to current investments. This balanced approach builds security, reduces liabilities, and maintains investment momentum. Once your emergency fund is complete and high-interest debt is eliminated, you can redirect full surplus to investments and house savings.
recommendations.suggested_action: Review debt interest rates; allocate $500/month to debts above 6% APR while building emergency fund

recommendations.title: Continue with VTTSX Target-Date Fund for Simplicity
recommendations.summary: Your VTTSX holding is well-suited for a beginner investor seeking hands-off diversification aligned with long-term goals.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: VTTSX (Vanguard Target Retirement 2065) is an excellent choice for your situation: it provides automatic diversification across global stocks and bonds, requires no active management, has low fees (~0.08% expense ratio), and automatically adjusts to become more conservative as you approach retirement. For a beginner investor with limited experience, this single-fund approach eliminates complex rebalancing decisions while maintaining broad market exposure. The fund's 2065 target date aligns reasonably with your long-term needs (you'd be 63 in 2065). No changes needed to this holding—simply continue contributions once your emergency fund is complete.
recommendations.suggested_action: Continue holding VTTSX; increase contributions after emergency fund completion
